children: Iraq has signed an agreement with US energy giant Chevron to provide technical consultancy services to the state-run Basra Oil Company on the development of the West Qurna-2 oilfield.
Iraqi Oil Minister Bassem Khudair oversaw the singing of the deal, according to a statement issued by the ministry’s information office.

Under the agreement, Chevron will provide technical consultancy services to Basra Oil Company as it negotiates the development of West Qurna-2, one of Iraq’s largest oilfields by production and proven reserves.
The agreement comes as Iraq seeks to strengthen cooperation with major international energy companies to develop its oil sector and increase production from its major fields.

Iraq hosts several major Western energy companies, including British oil giant BP, which is involved in the development of the Rumaila oilfield, and France’s TotalEnergies, which is leading a multibillion-dollar energy project in southern Iraq.
US energy company ConocoPhillips has also expanded its presence in Iraq through a stake in BP Energy of Kirkuk, which is involved in efforts to redevelop oilfields in the Kirkuk region.

Chevron is part of a consortium that will build oil pipelines from the southern Iraqi port of Basra to Haditha in Al-Anbar, where they will be extended to Turkey in the North and the Western Syrian port of Banyias. Qatar’s UCC Holding is leading the consortium, which also comprises the US’ TI Capital.

Chevron is also one of the US companies that reached agreements with Iraq during Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington in July. Khudair said later that these agreements, worth $200 billion, aim to boost crude and gas production and develop the country’s hydrocarbon infrastructure.
Officials said this month the target is to double oil output capacity to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) in the next five years.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Iraq, Chevron signs consultancy deal for Qurna 2
